question: Does the column-band order (order="bands") beat the recursive XY-cut order on pages with columns, full-width headers and full-width captions?

modes.bands: column bands: anything-to-text lineify / detectColumnCuts / orderByColumns

metric: Kendall's tau over matched GT lines (predicted order vs true order); coverage = matched GT lines / GT lines

text_in_order: Notes on Column Layout
The detector finds text as blobs of probability and the
layout step turns those blobs into lines that a reader
would follow. Each line is a rotated rectangle, and the
rectangle is then widened by the unclip ratio so that
the glyphs are fully covered. Columns are found from
the widest vertical gap that runs through every box on
the page, and rows inside a column are read from the
top, one row at a time, from left to right.
A paragraph break is a horizontal gap larger than a
single line, so the lines of one paragraph stay in one
block and the blocks follow each other in reading
order. Small gaps between words on one line are
bridged when fragments share a baseline band.
